Criminal Appeal No. 4923 of 1991 (Dhaka)
Criminal Appeal No. 87 of 1986 (Rangpur)
lawyer:
Muhammad Ayenuddin, Advocate -------- For the Appellant.
Abdus Salam Mamun, AAG  -------- For the State.
parties:
Rajab Ali Zulfiqar  -------- Appellant.
Vs.
State   -------- Respondent.
full_judgment: The learned Advocate for the appellant in support of his application contends that in view of section 428 of CrPC there is no bar in receipt of additional evidence in the appellate Court; only requirement for that is that in allowing such application for additional evidence, the court shall record its reasons with a finding that such additional evidence is necessary in the interest of justice. He further submits that as the appellant could not appear in court at the trial or engage any lawyer for him, he failed to produce the said document as an explanation for the entire amount of money he was entrusted with. Therefore at this stage, for the ends of justice, this application for admitting the paper-document as an additional evidence should be allowed. The learned AAG, on the other hand, seriously opposes the application for additional evidence at this stage filed on behalf of the accused appellant who has been tried in absentia as he was absconding from the very beginning to the end of the trial and even thereafter until he was arrested and taken into custody on 2.3.86. He further submits that this provision under section 428 CrPC, if read in its entirety, will show that it is in fact meant mainly for the purpose of the prosecution upon which the sole burden of proof of the case entirely rests. In the instant case, the application under section 428 CrPC has not come from the prosecution side but from the side of the accused appellant who has been tried in absentia and on whose behalf there is no evidence on record. He being an absconder could not either cross-examine the PWs or lead any evidence for his defence and as such there cannot be any question of additional evidence which presupposes existence of some evidence already recorded on behalf of the party concerned. The learned AAG therefore contends that this application on behalf of the accused appellant is not at all maintainable and is liable to be outright rejected. Mr. Ayenuddin, the learned Advocate for the appellant, in support of his contention .has however relied on some decisions reported in 4 DLR (SC) 551, 5 DLR (WP) 13 and 7 DLR (FC) 1.
